proof_summary: For integers above the two cutoffs, a witness directly gives a Goldbach decomposition in the even case and a Lemoine decomposition in the odd case; explicit finite tables supply the decompositions below the cutoffs. For cousin primes, if all admissible smaller primes \(q\) were bounded, taking \(n=2N!\) beyond that bound would force the witness’s \(q\mid n\) and hence \(q\mid(n-q)\); primality then gives \(n-q=q\), contradicting the required strict inequality \(2q<n\).
